blocks.text: Netweb designs, assembles and deploys high-end computing systems - supercomputing/HPC clusters, private cloud and hyperconverged (HCI) stacks, GPU-based AI systems, high-performance storage and data-centre servers - under its Tyrone brand, bundling in-house middleware and cloud software [F] (AR2026 p.9) (PPT Aug 2026). It buys the silicon (GPUs, CPUs, memory, flash) from NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Samsung, designs boards and systems, integrates and tests them in Faridabad, and sells them as a one-time capex purchase to the customer; it does not run data centres or sell annuity cloud services [F] (AR2026 p.9) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) (CALL Jan 2026). Revenue is overwhelmingly product sale recognised at a point in time: Rs 2,132.2 cr of goods and Rs 51.4 cr of services in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.118).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. Valuation is disconnected from any modelled outcome: the reverse DCF requires ~87.2% annual sales growth for five years against 19.8% in the base case; even the bull DCF value (Rs 1,026.5) is 77.7% below the Rs 4,613 price [E] (NUMBERS).

2. Cash conversion is far weaker than our statements data shows: the annual report's FY26 operating cash flow is Rs 171.5 cr, not Rs 790 cr; the cash-flow statement prints the receivables change as a positive Rs 309.2 cr when receivables actually rose, and the gap (Rs 618.5 cr) is exactly twice that line [F] (AR2026 p.101) (NUMBERS) [E].

3. FY26 operating cash flow depended on customer advances: advances from customers rose from Rs 2.5 cr to Rs 412.8 cr; without them FY26 CFO would have been negative [F] (AR2026 p.101) (AR2026 p.117) [E].

4. Working capital is ballooning: inventory rose from Rs 221.3 cr to Rs 804.8 cr (raw materials Rs 761.9 cr) in FY26, and free cash fell from Rs 406.6 cr to Rs 73.4 cr in Q1 FY27 as net debt turned to Rs 199.9 cr [F] (AR2026 p.112) (PPT Aug 2026).

5. Concentration is rising, not falling: three customers above 10% of revenue; top-5 share rose to ~62% in FY26 on our reconstruction; 28.8% of sales went through 3 dealers [F] (AR2026 p.123) (AR2026 p.75) [AI] (AR2026 p.24).
6. The AI growth is a handful of government-linked strategic orders executed through empanelled intermediaries; 42.8% of revenue is government [F] (AR2026 p.5) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

7. Disclosure definitions keep moving: strategic vs organic reporting was dropped in Q1 FY27 and the pipeline now merges both, so like-for-like tracking is impossible; management said it did not have the comparable number [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

8. Gross margin is compressing as AI mix rises: 20.85% in FY26 vs 23.11% in FY25; strategic orders carry 150-200 bp lower PBT margin by management's own guidance [F] (AR2026 p.36) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

9. Promoters sold ~20.98 lakh shares in FY26 and holding fell 4.05 points in a year, while promoters personally guarantee and collateralise the new bank debt; an enabling resolution to raise capital is in place [F] (AR2026 p.114) (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.116) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

10. Input control is nil: silicon is bought from a few vendors (top three ~65-70% of procurement per the rating agency) mostly imported from Taiwan; memory prices are rising and not expected to soften for a year [F] (RATING) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

Is AI revenue recurring or a one-off tranche? Bulls: management says 'strategic is the new normal' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Bears: ~Rs 1,014 cr of the Rs 2,184 cr strategic orders was executed by Q1 FY27 and ~Rs 1,170 cr remains [E]; no new strategic order value has been disclosed since Nov 2025 [AI].

Is the pipeline a leading indicator? It more than doubled to Rs 10,410 cr, but only because strategic opportunities were added to it; the ex-strategic pipeline was Rs 4,400 cr in May [MC] (CALL May 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) [AI].

Are margins structural? 13-15% EBITDA margins have held for five years [F] (NUMBERS), but gross margin fell 226 bp in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.36); the market may be over-crediting pricing power, or under-crediting operating leverage that offset gross-margin dilution [AI].

Is working capital a hedge or a risk? Management calls inventory a hedge against component shortages [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); the balance sheet shows Rs 761.9 cr of raw materials at March and net debt by June [F] (AR2026 p.112) (PPT Aug 2026).

Is the stock a capacity story? Management says capability, not capacity, drives the business and facilities support Rs 3,000+ cr turnover [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); Q1 FY27 annualised revenue is already ~Rs 3,280 cr [E].

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus narrative treats Netweb as a compounding sovereign-AI platform with clean cash conversion (our own rule-based screen flags 'profits turn into cash' at 2.01x over three years). On the annual report's own cash-flow statement, three-year CFO is ~Rs 176 cr against ~Rs 396 cr of PAT (~0.45x) [E] (AR2026 p.101) (NUMBERS), and FY26 cash was supported by customer advances that reversed in Q1 FY27. The business is a good, capital-light system integrator with real engineering, but its reported growth is concentrated in a few government-linked AI orders routed through intermediaries, working-capital intensive, and priced at levels (Rs 4,613 vs bull DCF Rs 1,026.5) that no scenario in our model supports [F] (NUMBERS). The variant view is that the risk is less 'will AI demand continue' and more 'what happens to cash, margins and the multiple when order lumpiness returns'.
